articles.title: Rising UK consumer confidence gives Andy Burnham ‘golden opportunity’, survey says – business live
articles.snippet: BRC says confidence in economy hits highest level since the lows reached at start of Iran war In Germany, factory gate inflation hit a three-year high in July, adding to signs of fresh inflationary pressures in Europe’s largest economy. Prices charged by manufacturers for their goods, ranging from food to cars and tools, climbed 3% year on year last month following June’s 1.8% rise, Germany’s statistics office said . Economists had expected an increase to 2.7%. Conditions at the early stages of the inflationary surge have suddenly become uncomfortable. The war involving Iran is leaving its mark, as it the heat. Continue reading...

articles.title: Protest in Essen tegen windturbine van 197 meter hoog: "Twee keer de Boerentoren? Niet in landelijk gebied!"
articles.snippet: In Essen is er protest tegen de komst van een windmolen van 197 meter hoog op een weiland aan de wijk Schriek. 550 mensen ondertekenden een petitie tegen die plannen. Daarom heeft de federale overheidsdienst Binnenlandse Zaken het nummer 1722 geactiveerd. Daarmee kunnen mensen die hulp nodig hebben voor stormschade of wateroverlast de brandweer bereiken.

articles.title: 91 banen bedreigd bij afvalverwerker Renewi, merendeel bij vestiging in Lommel
articles.snippet: Bij afvalverwerker Renewi staan 91 banen op de helling, waarvan het grootste deel bij de vestiging in Lommel. Dat bevestigen vakbonden en directie na een bijzondere ondernemingsraad vanochtend. Renewi is marktleider in ons land voor het ophalen en recycleren van bedrijfsafval. Van de 91 bedreigde banen zitten er 61 bij het Shared Service Center in Lommel.

articles.title: ‘We now live without this violence’: the Colombian farmers giving up coca for palm oil
articles.snippet: Subsidies and a crackdown on armed groups are helping smallholders rebuild their lives, leaving behind decades of conflict and fear Surrounded by towering oil palm trees on his farm in the small village of Caño Barbú, near San Pablo in northern Colombia , Yoger Payares uses a malayo – a pole-mounted iron tool with a hook – to hack at the fronds of one, freeing a bunch of its vibrant reddish-orange fruit so it falls to the ground. Today, Payares proudly works in the oil palm industry. But for more than a decade, just yards away, he grew coca leaves, becoming embroiled in the illicit industry in 1990 after leaving his job as a cattle farmer. Continue reading...

articles.title: Tourists on pastry quest overrun scenic spot in Italian mountains

The visitors ventured en masse to the Friedrich August refuge – perched at 2,300 metres (7,500ft) above sea level, between Col Rodella and Passo Sella in Val di Fassa – some reportedly waking up at dawn or camping overnight, just to ensure they could buy a freshly baked krapfen , a traditional German pastry similar to a doughnut, before they ran out. articles.snippet: Annie Kelly heads to Brick Lane to hear from residents campaigning against a massive datacentre on one of London’s most famous streets Brick Lane is one of the most vibrant and best-known streets in London. articles.title: US states accuse Meta of covering up research on teen social media addiction in pivotal trial
articles.snippet: State attorneys general claim tech company intentionally designed addictive products that harm young people Lawyers representing 29 US states have accused Meta of covering up internal research showing Instagram was addictive for teenagers. In a packed courtroom Tuesday, on the opening day of a landmark legal challenge, they said the company knew its products harmed children but hid that information from the public. “I heard from many of you at jury selection that the health and wellbeing of kids is a shared responsibility,” said Megan O’Neill, a deputy attorney general for California, in her opening statements. “Meta didn’t do its share.” Continue reading...
